source.title: Scaling Remote Sensing Foundation Models: Data Domain Tradeoffs at the Peta-Scale
source.authors: Charith Wickrema; Eliza Mace; H. Brown; Heidys Cabrera; N. Krall; M. O'Neill; Shivangi Sarkar; Lowell Weissman; Eric Hughes; Guido Zarrella

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests data and parameter scaling of vision foundation models in remote sensing imagery, an extension to a non-text modality; it does not test language-model scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper reports remote-sensing validation-loss fits against dataset size and parameter count. Batch-size and learning-rate results are not rows because they do not test the listed claim versions. The dataset-size fit changes substantially when runs trapped in a local minimum are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of validation loss against dataset size and parameter count for ViT remote-sensing image pretraining. These are its own results on whether the scaling form carries to a non-text modality (V5). The dataset-size fit changes sharply depending on which runs are included, which bears on V7. It does not check any extrapolated prediction, so V2 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that loss falls as a diminishing-returns power law in dataset size, after excluding trapped runs. Parameter scaling is flat under their fixed budget, which they read as a data-limited regime partly confounded by tokens-per-parameter.
record.recipe_differences: Uses vision-transformer remote-sensing pretraining and validation loss, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling; varies image dataset size and backbone size, not parameters, tokens, and compute jointly.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset-size fit quality depends on excluding runs trapped in a local minimum. Parameter-scaling conclusions are under a fixed training budget, identical steps, and batch size; the authors note the resulting change in tokens per parameter.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Pattern Recognition
record.problems: The preferred data-scaling fit excludes approximately half of the runs that became trapped in a local minimum; the all-trials fit has R2 = 0.18. The reported data-scaling fit uses three converged scales, and the paper does not report held-out prediction validation. The parameter-scaling comparison holds steps and batch size fixed, so larger models receive fewer training tokens per parameter; the authors identify this as a confound. No uncertainty intervals for the fitted exponents are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for batch-size and learning-rate experiments: they do not measure the claim versions. No individual backbone loss rows are provided because the paper reports nearly indistinguishable curves and an aggregate fitted parameter-scaling result rather than separate textual loss values.

untested.parts: No fitted law is checked against a larger held-out run.
Depth and width are not varied at fixed parameter count.

Only remote-sensing EO imagery under ScaleMAE. Video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested. Compute scaling is not tested, and parameter scaling is only tested in a data-limited fixed-budget regime.
Downstream tasks are not evaluated; the authors list this as future work.
Parameter counting, schedule choices and fitting method are not compared. Only the choice of which runs to include is shown to matter.

missing.what: Which three dataset sizes converged, and the per-size converged loss values behind the Figure 9 fits

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 label should be dropped: no extrapolation is validated, and r1 was never linked to V2. The parameter-scaling null should not be read as a challenge, because the authors themselves flag the fixed-budget confound and the data bottleneck. The data-scaling evidence is thin: three points, a very small exponent, and no confidence intervals.

versions.untested_parts: Tests vision models on remote-sensing imagery, not held-out pretraining loss of language models.
Reports fitted dataset-size trends but does not validate predictions against a held-out run or a run beyond the fitted range.
Does not find a loss-minimising parameters-and-tokens allocation at fixed compute or compare allocation trends across compute budgets.
Does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at a fixed parameter count.
Tests remote-sensing image data and parameter scaling; does not test other modalities such as video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Does not test downstream task performance or its predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
Demonstrates sensitivity of the dataset-size fit to excluding trapped trials. Does not compare parameter-counting methods or compute-optimal allocation fits across setups.

rows.subject: ScaleMAE ViT-G (ViT-Giant)
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss against dataset size, excluding the three runs that surpassed the local minimum.

conditions.value: 5k–1M full images; the converged fit uses three scales

rows.measure: Converged validation loss versus dataset size; fitted power law L(N) = A + BN^-a, with a = 0.03 and R2 = 0.941 (figure reports R2 = 0.94).
rows.note: The text says the fit is based on three scales ranging from 5k–1M samples; Figure 9 identifies the converged fit as three trials. The paper presents the trend as supporting extrapolation, but does not report an out-of-sample prediction check.
rows.check: The link is right. The fit rests on only three converged trials, and the paper does not say which dataset sizes they are. The exponent of 0.03 is very shallow, and the fitted floor A of about 1.7e-07 makes this effectively a pure power law. There are no uncertainty bounds.

source_check.correct: Retain the three trials that surpassed the local minimum; exclude the three trapped trials. The retained-trial fit has a = 0.03 and R2 = 0.941 in the prose, rounded to 0.94 in Figure 9.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5.3, pp. 15–16; Figure 9 and caption, p. 18.
source_check.problem: The operation reverses the selection rule by saying the three successful trials were excluded; the condition field correctly says trapped trials were excluded.

rows.subject: ScaleMAE ViT-G (ViT-Giant)
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss against dataset size, including all six dataset-size trials.
rows.measure: Validation loss versus dataset size; figure fit R2 = 0.18, with equation y = 3.9e-07 + 0.7·x^-0.03.
rows.value: R2 = 0.18; fitted exponent shown as -0.03 in the figure equation
rows.note: The text states that approximately half the runs became trapped after the first 5k steps and that these points were excluded from the preferred fit. The all-trials fit had poor correspondence. No out-of-sample larger-run prediction is reported.
rows.check: Remove V2. The row checks no extrapolated prediction; the figure caption's claim that the fit enables extrapolation is the authors' assertion, not a test. The poor fit (R2 = 0.18) comes from runs stuck in an early local minimum, which is an optimisation failure rather than a property of the data scaling.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.4; Figure 8, p. 17; Figure 9 and caption, p. 18.

rows.subject: ViT-Base, ViT-Large, ViT-Huge, and ViT-Giant (aggregate parameter-scaling sweep)
rows.stage_stated: pretraining; framework not stated for this experiment
rows.operation_detail: Vary backbone parameter count while holding dataset, schedule, and optimizer fixed.

conditions.value: fixed budget; identical steps and batch size

rows.measure: Converged validation loss versus parameter count; estimated exponent b ≈ 0; Figure 11 fit: y = 3.3e-04 + 2.7e-04·x^-5.3e-06, R2 = -5.83e-03.
rows.note: The paper reports the sweep’s curves as nearly indistinguishable and the fitted slope as statistically indistinguishable from zero. Individual loss values for each backbone are not stated. The authors note that fixed steps and batch size give larger models fewer training tokens per parameter.
rows.check: Remove V7: the row does not vary any fitting choice. Steps and batch size were fixed at Akupara-100k, which the authors call a data-limited regime with fewer tokens per parameter for larger models. So the version's premise that the other factors are not the bottleneck is not met. The text gives 630M for ViT-Huge but Figure 10 says 632M. Figure 10's axis says training loss while its caption says validation loss.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased, but the preferred fit uses only three selected trials and no held-out extrapolation test. Source inconsistencies: ViT-Huge is 630M in Section 4.5 versus 632M in Figure 10; Figure 10's axis says training loss while its caption says validation loss.

statements.correction: ScaleMAE data fit: R2 = 0.941 after excluding trapped trials; R2 = 0.18 for all six trials. Fixed-budget parameter sweep: b ≈ 0 on Akupara-100k. Convergence selection and resource balance qualify scope; V5 label = limits_scope for these conditions.
statements.problem: The study-specific numbers and descriptions are correct, but the challenges label overstates evidence from optimization failures and a data-limited parameter sweep.
